proposals.name: Lens magnifying red background source
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens is slowly aligning with a red background source, achromatically magnifying it above a steady blended baseline. The g-r colour has stayed near 1.1 mag while the flux rose roughly sevenfold over 30 days and flattened near peak, unlike a Type Ia explosion template.
proposals.predicts: The flux will now decline in g and r together, mirroring the rise with essentially unchanged g-r colour and returning to the constant baseline, rather than cooling, reddening and decaying as a Type Ia would.

proposals.name: Galactic microlensing event
proposals.idea: An unseen point-mass lens in the low-latitude Galactic plane is magnifying a red background star, producing the slow, months-long rise seen since day -30. This is gravitational magnification rather than an explosion, so there is no ejecta cooling or radioactive evolution.
proposals.predicts: The light curve will peak and then decline symmetrically with the same timescale in g and r at constant g-r color, returning to the constant baseline, unlike a SN Ia which predicts an asymmetric, color-evolving decline.

proposals.name: Drifting calibration subtraction residual
proposals.idea: A slowly drifting zero-point and template-subtraction residual in this crowded low-latitude field adds spurious flux at a fixed position. Its steady growth mimics a smooth, nearly colour-stable brightening in both g and r with no real transient onset.
proposals.predicts: It predicts the flux keeps rising linearly in microjansky per day in both bands with constant colour, showing no supernova peak, turnover, or cooling.

proposals.name: Microlensed red source
proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point lens is magnifying a steady red background source, rather than a Type Ia explosion fading after peak. The achromatic lensing magnification explains the month-long rise in both bands at nearly constant g-r colour that the Ia forecast increasingly underpredicted.
proposals.predicts: The g and r fluxes will peak together and then decline symmetrically with the same tE and unchanged g-r colour, instead of the asymmetric, colour-evolving decline of a supernova.

proposals.name: Microlensed red background star
proposals.idea: The >30-day, nearly colour-constant (g-r~1.1) brightening at low Galactic latitude is the achromatic magnification of a red background star by an unseen foreground lens, not an explosion. The fitted Ia peaked and faded too early because magnification keeps rising toward closest approach long after a supernova would turn over.
proposals.predicts: It predicts a symmetric, achromatic turnover followed by a decline mirroring the rise back to the constant baseline, with g-r unchanged through peak and no supernova-like cooling or rapid post-peak fade.
